subject: Post-call: FinMetrics inference cost constraints & pilot criteria
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Brighton <alex.brighton@finmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: FinMetrics inference cost constraints & pilot criteria

Alex — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to follow up on.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Monthly inference spend has risen suddenly (~$85k/month) and variability is causing budget surprise.
- High tail latency for some batch jobs causing timeouts in downstream analytics.
- Lack of telemetry for per-endpoint token distribution — hard to identify heavy prompts.

Current stack you described:
- Front-end -> internal API -> OpenAI hosted endpoints for generation (Davinci variants)
- Some local microservices handling post-processing; no dedicated GPU fleet today

Success criteria (what would make this pilot a win for FinMetrics):
1) Reduce per-token unit cost by >=30% on the busiest endpoints while maintaining quality (no regressions on the 12 test prompts you shared).
2) P95 response latency < 300ms for the 80% of interactive traffic during business hours.
3) Clear visibility on token distribution and cost attribution by route.

Technical openness we noted:
- You are open to model quantization and smaller (open) model variants if quality holds.
- Willing to trial batching for async jobs but interactive endpoints must remain low-latency.

Next steps I propose (for alignment):
- Redwood will draft a short pilot scope with suggested inference configuration (batching profile for async jobs, KV cache thresholds, quantization profile candidates).
- You’ll share: (a) sample traffic traces (anonymized request logs or token histograms), (b) the 12 evaluation prompts + success thresholds, (c) procurement contacts for scope/terms.
- Schedule a 30-min ops sync to align telemetry access and plan a 6-week pilot.

Let me know if I misstated anything. I’ll loop in Diego (infrastructure) and Marissa (cost & pilot ops) for the pilot plan.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Irene — great recap, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and numbers: 

Clarifications / data points:
- Current monthly spend is ~USD 85k (generation-only). Embeddings and retriever costs are separate.
- Peak interactive traffic is 1.2k RPS across Europe + US; typical business-hour sustained is ~350 RPS.
- Async batch jobs (ETL-style re-encodings) account for ~40% of token volume and can tolerate up to 2s extra latency.

About quality: we can provide the 12 prompts + a small blind eval set (50 samples) — target is that top-level metrics (ROUGE-like business scoring) do not drop >5%.

Telemetry: procurement will need a brief note on what logs/access will be provided. I can get that to you by EOD Friday.

Procurement contact: procurement@finmetrics.com (cc'd in this thread). Expect some legal review re: data retention; they prefer KMS/HSM notes up front.

Happy to proceed with the pilot plan you suggested. Can we aim to kick off the ops sync next week?

Thanks,
Alex Brighton
Head of Platform Engineering | FinMetrics

Looping in our operational plan from the cost/engineering side — Diego and I sketched a practical pilot that minimizes risk: 

Pilot outline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: access & telemetry — FinMetrics provides anonymized token histograms + sample traces (S3 link or direct upload).
- Week 1-2: baseline run on Redwood hosted trial with matched prompts (no routing changes) to measure current unit economics.
- Week 3-4: incremental rollout of batching for async jobs (configurable batch windows), enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts. Measure cost/delta.
- Week 5-6: candidate quantized model test (A/B on a small percentage of traffic) to validate quality delta.

Open engineering asks:
- Will FinMetrics provide a staging endpoint or can we route a mirrored subset of traffic? Mirroring is preferred to avoid production risk.
- Token histogram format: prefer CSV with columns [route, avg_tokens, p50, p90, p99].

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Weekly cost/readout deck (cost per 1k tokens by route), runbook for rollback, and suggested SLA targets if scaled.

Next internal ops step: Diego, can you confirm an initial batching profile (target window 50–150ms for async) and a suggested quant profile (4-bit candidate) by tomorrow? I can draft the initial pilot scope doc once we have that.

-Marissa
